question: What will the first reported earnings per share after September 2026 be for the following companies? (Apple)

calls.reasoning: Guidance build (rev +9-11% on $102.5B, GM 47-48% incl ~1pt tariff refund, opex $19.1-19.4B, OI&E $0.35B, tax 16.5%, ~14.5B diluted shares) gives ~$1.99 at midpoint, ~$2.06 at top end. Consensus ~$1.98-2.02 with net downward revisions. Apple has beaten nine straight quarters, recent beats ~4-7%, so median set slightly above consensus at ~$2.06. Downside risks: memory '100-year flood' costs and worsening supply constraints. Market check: Polymarket lists Apple EPS-beat markets (earlier quarters had $2.67 and $1.89 thresholds), but no page was opened for this quarter, so no price is used; no Kalshi market found; bookmakers not checked.

- Downside items: reports of iPhone 18 Pro production cuts, supply constraints, memory costs, swings in minority-investment marks.
- Markets: Polymarket runs Apple 'beat EPS' markets (past thresholds $2.67 and $1.89); no market page was opened for this quarter. No Kalshi market found.

calls.reconciliation: Disputes: (1) report date Oct 29 vs Nov 2. Two runs cite Apple's Nov 2 confirmation; it can't be verified offline and doesn't affect the value. (2) Guidance-midpoint EPS $1.92 vs $1.99. I recomputed it using the implied 14.75B FQ3 share count less buybacks (~14.65B) and got ~$1.97 mid, ~$2.04 top. Run 2's build was too low and Run 1's share count (14.5B) too small. (3) Size of the beat is judgment. Beat history argues ~$2.07-2.13, while revisions and memory/supply headwinds argue lower. I take ~$2.05, near the top of guidance. I accept the runs' reference class and ~0.16-0.19 dispersion, widened slightly to 0.20 for the GAAP tax-charge risk.
